applicability: Applies to expressions given as an ordered list of integer operands (length 1 to 8, each between -10 and 20) and a list of binary operators from {+,-,*} of length exactly len(operands)-1. It counts distinct numerical values over all full parenthesizations preserving operand and operator order, counting each distinct value once. It does not handle other operators, reordering, unary operators, non-integer operands, or inputs outside the stated bounds; such inputs raise ValueError.
description: Interval dynamic programming over the operand sequence. For each contiguous interval [i,j], maintain the set of all integer values obtainable by fully parenthesizing that subexpression while preserving order. Base case: a single operand yields its own value. For longer intervals, for every split point k, combine every value from the left interval with every value from the right interval using the operator at position k, and union the results. The answer is the cardinality of the set for the full interval. Exact integer arithmetic is used, so no floating-point error occurs. The main uncertainty is performance if intermediate sets grow large, but with at most 8 operands and small integer bounds this is negligible.
